canon: Grunda gave her name and said the King sent her.
Grunda took a stone from Cob before he could throw it; she did not hurt him.
Cob stamped once and the left boot crackled.
Cob refused Grunda's request to look in the boot and backed toward the water butt.
Moll dropped from the wall and stood between Grunda and Cob, telling her to keep her hands off his boots.
Kell recorded Grunda's request and Cob's refusal.
Grunda took a stone from Cob before he could throw it; Cob still has other stones.
Cob claims the oversized boots are his father's and says he found them.
The left boot crackles when Cob stamps.
Moll dropped down from the wall and stood between Grunda and Cob when Grunda asked to inspect the boot.
Kell recorded Grunda's name and the disputed boots, then recorded her request to inspect the boot and Cob's refusal.
Grunda's attempt to haul Prout down barely moved the rope; it runs over the beam and is fastened somewhere inside the loft.
Kell addressed Grunda as the King's investigator and said they would need a ladder or access to the loft.
A pigeon was perched on the hoist beam.
A stone struck the hoist hook.
Dragging the water butt sloshed water over its rim.
Kell steadied the water butt while Grunda climbed onto it.
Grunda dragged the full water butt beneath Prout and climbed up within reach; Kell steadied it.
Prout has a slanting rope mark and a separate level line around his throat; Grunda identified the level line as strangulation before he was hoisted.
Kell agreed to sign Prout in as a murder, but will not write a name without evidence.

transition.when: Grunda searches behind the water butt for another way into the loft.

check.reason: to find a way into the loft and spot signs of what happened there
check.success: She finds the loose board behind the water butt and squeezes into the loft. The smashed lantern, spilled ink, heel-scuffs leading from the tally desk to the barred door, and the hoist rope's docker's knot show a struggle and a staged hanging.
check.failure: She finds no way in behind the water butt.

patches.why: The prepared loose board offers a way into the loft without requiring the locked yard doors, a ladder, or the warden's key; its prepared signs can break the suicide story.

repairs.assessment: Grunda is pursuing the crackling boot with a gentle approach, and the failed check has made Cob defensive without shutting the scene down. The children are reacting actively; give her room to change tack rather than repeat the same ask.
repairs.notes: Cob has refused this look; don't make him surrender the boot or repeat the same check. A kindness with nothing asked back, or a promise that truly answers his fear, can open a different path. Keep his name and the boot safe unless Grunda earns his trust.

repairs.assessment: Grunda is trying to treat the body respectfully and has shifted toward investigating it after the boy refused her request. The failed attempt has revealed a real access problem, but play is still moving and the children remain engaged.
repairs.notes: Don’t repeat the ladder obstacle as a dead end; let Grunda choose another avenue, and keep the children responsive without making them give up secrets for free.

repairs.assessment: Grunda is improvising practical ways to reach the body and treating the children gently despite Cob’s refusal. The scene is moving well: she’s now close enough to inspect the body, and the clues already shown have established that this was no suicide.

Grunda found a physical sign of murder and Kell has accepted it, so the scene has moved cleanly into the investigation. The player is enjoying practical, forceful problem-solving and is actively pursuing the truth.
